You are a group discussion leader. Your have to discuss with real robots (agents) to break an overall task to smaller subtasks and assign a subtask to each agent.The agents are described below:

"""
"ur5_1" is a  "UR5" agent. It has the following capabilities:

"""
The followinfg is a list of python dicts describing the robot's capabilities:
 - Mobility capability: {"summary": "Stationary six-joint arm on a pedestal; no mobile base."}
 - Manipulation capability: {"summary": "The EAI host exposes a Cartesian pick and place skill for a workbench carton using idealized follow-proxy attachment. This is not contact grasping. Success is evaluated after simulation; no prior success is assumed.", "base_position_native_xzy": [0, 0.45, 0], "joint_count": 6}

"""


"""

You should assign subtasks to each agent based on their capabilities, following this format:

{robot_id||subtask_description}\n\nRemember you must include the brackets and you MUST include ALL the |robots| and |goal conditions| in your response.
Even if you think a robot should not assign a subtask, you should assign it with {robot_id||Nothing to do}.
Even if you think a robot should assign multiple subtasks, you should combine them into one {robot_id||subtask_description} format.
Remember the subtask target should always include 'objects', DO NOT include 'region' in |subtask description|.

The task is described below:

"""
Pick and place the workbench carton
"""

All agents are in a scene, the scene description is as follows:

"""
Declared isolated UR5 workbench fixture, before physics execution. Coordinates are native [x,z,y], height second. UR5 arm base is [0,0.45,0]. The workbench carton object /World/Object is at [0.45,0.475,0]; its place destination is [0.425,0.475,0.01]. The host provides its Cartesian pick and place skill with idealized follow-proxy attachment. Physical success has not been measured.
"""

Now you should assign subtasks to each agent based on their capabilities, following the format in the system prompt.
{ur5_1||Pick up the objects workbench carton at [0.45,0.475,0] and place it at [0.425,0.475,0.01] using the Cartesian pick-and-place skill.}
